chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rib'i, from Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who is appointed as executor of a will. He said: If it was sent to him from a city (far away), then he does not have the right to refuse it. But if he was in a city where someone else can be found (to serve as executor), then that is up to him.

key_terms.رَدُّهَا: Rejection or refusal of the executorship appointment
key_terms.مِصْرٍ: City or populated center where multiple qualified individuals may reside
key_terms.يُوصَى إِلَيْهِ: The one appointed as executor/trustee of a will (al-wasi ilayhi); the person designated to carry out the deceased's wishes

ai.seo_question: Can a person refuse to be named executor of a will in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules on the legal obligation of a person designated as executor (wasi) of a will. The ruling distinguishes two scenarios: when the appointment was sent from a distant city — making refusal impermissible because the testator may have had no other viable choice — versus when the appointed executor is locally available alongside other qualified individuals, in which case refusal is permitted. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of balancing personal autonomy with communal obligation in matters of trust.
word_analysis: who is appointed as executor (of a will)

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazal Bin Shazaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Rabie, from Fuzayl,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man whose appointment as an executor (of will) was sent to him’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was sent to him from (the same) city, so it is not up to him to reject it, and if it was from a city in which someone else can be found, so that is up to him’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated it from al-Fadf ibn Shadhan, from ibn abu ‘Umayr, from Rib‘iy, from Fudayl

who has narrated the following: “It is about the case of a man who is appointed in a will as the executor a will. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If the appointment is sent to him from another town he cannot refuse to accept the appointment, but if it is from the same town then it is up to him to accept or reject it.’”
